standard_prerequisites.name: Propositional truncation
standard_prerequisites.statement: brck X is the propositional truncation of X, and a goal that is a mere proposition may be proved by assuming an element of X.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the technique applied at source lines 89, 103 and 113.

standard_prerequisites.name: Unique choice
standard_prerequisites.statement: To construct an object with a propositional existence statement one may instead characterise it uniquely and prove that the characterisation is inhabited.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the technique named at source lines 97-99 that leads to the auxiliary type B(x).

standard_prerequisites.name: Transport in identity and function types
standard_prerequisites.statement: Transport along a path in an identity type, and in a function type, reduces to componentwise statements.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is used at source line 107 to reduce the identification of h with h' to a pointwise equation.

core_obligations: From the given g : prd x:A brck(a = x) show first that every path type x = y is a set: truncation induction produces p : a = x and p' : a = y, composing with p and opp p' gives an equivalence (x = y) ~ (a = a), and a = a is a set by hypothesis (source lines 87-92).

Explain that the naive definition f(x) := opp(g x) `ct` q `ct` g x is unavailable because g(x) is only a truncated path, and replace it by the characterisation B(x) := Sigma r : x = x, prd s : a = x, r = opp s `ct` q `ct` s (source lines 94-101).

Show that each B(x) is a mere proposition: truncation induction gives p : a = x, and for (r,h) and (r',h') in B(x) the path h(p) `ct` opp(h'(p)) identifies r with r', the remaining coherence reducing by transport in identity and function types to an equality between elements of the set x = x (source lines 102-110).

Inhabit B(x) for every x: truncation induction gives p : a = x, the candidate is r := opp p `ct` q `ct` p, and the required identity reduces to q `ct` (p `ct` opp s) = (p `ct` opp s) `ct` q, which is the centrality hypothesis (source lines 112-117).
Conclude that prd x:A B(x) holds and read off the required f with f(a) = q (source lines 84 and 112-117).

proof_roadmap.step: Show that all path types of A are sets.
Replace the unavailable naive definition by the unique characterisation B(x).
Show B(x) is a mere proposition.
Inhabit B(x) using the centrality hypothesis.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `lem:autohtpy` at source lines 77-85: if a = a is a set, every x : A is merely equal to a, and q commutes with every self-path of a, then there is f : prd x:A (x = x) with f(a) = q. The author's proof (source lines 86-118) is one of the more delicate arguments of the chapter because the obvious definition cannot be written: g(x) inhabits a truncation and the target type x = x is not a proposition, so the proof first establishes that all path types of A are sets (lines 87-92), then replaces the naive formula by the uniquely characterised type B(x) (lines 94-101) and proves that B(x) is a mere proposition by a coherence argument that consumes transport in identity and function types (lines 102-110), and only then inhabits B(x) with the candidate opp p `ct` q `ct` p, whose verification reduces to the centrality hypothesis (lines 112-117). The statement exhibits none of the three stages and hides why the naive definition fails.
